findings.description: The real EARS-002 text only requires that per-row formulas reference their own row's cells from a fixed anchor beneath a frozen header — it says nothing about WHICH formulas exist or their arithmetic. The real code (lib.rs L563-591) and all three B-outputs pin an exact 13-column A–M schema with specific per-cell formulas: Market Value=`=E{r}*B{r}`, Unrealized P&L=`=F{r}-D{r}`, Est. Unrealized Tax=`=G{r}*H{r}`, Net Unrealized=`=G{r}*(1-H{r})`, Unrealized %=`=IF(D{r}=0,0,G{r}/D{r})`, Price=`=GOOGLEFINANCE("<ticker>","price")`. This entire formula catalogue is code+test-pinned (formula.rs) surplus with zero trace in the spec text.

Zero-basis division guard: Unrealized % is written as `=IF(D{r}=0,0,G{r}/D{r})` (lib.rs L570-574) rather than a bare `=G{r}/D{r}`. SHEET-FORMULA-002 never mentions a div-by-zero boundary rule; this is a code-only tie-break invisible in the spec text but pinned by all three B-reconstructions.

The Cell::Value/Cell::Formula typing split (Price, Market Value, Unrealized P&L, Est. Unrealized Tax, Net Unrealized, Unrealized %, Quote Date = Formula; Symbol, Shares, Avg Cost/Share, Total Basis, Est. Tax Rate, Realized P&L = Value) plus the load-bearing encoding trick that Est. Tax Rate must be written as a percent-suffixed VALUE string (e.g. "20.0000%") — never a formula — so Sheets coerces it to a numeric fraction consumable by `=G*H`/`=G*(1-H)` (lib.rs L439-449 doc, L584-585; formula.rs `est_tax_rate_cell_is_numeric_percent_the_posttax_formulas_can_multiply`) is entirely unstated by EARS-002, which never discusses value/formula typing or numeric-coercion contracts.

The Quote Date formula's exact locale-proof encoding — `=IFERROR(TEXT(INT(GOOGLEFINANCE("<ticker>","tradetime"))-DATE(1970,1,1),"0"),"")`, truncating trade-time to a date serial, re-basing to days-since-1970-01-01 (the kernel Date epoch), rendering via TEXT for locale invariance, and emitting empty string (never an error literal) on load/error (lib.rs L259-274; formula.rs `positions_carries_a_locale_proof_quote_date_companion_column`) — is a substantial code+test-pinned contract nowhere implied by SHEET-FORMULA-002's text.

The DuplicateSymbolRow defensive error: if `Snapshot.positions` ever yields two rows for one symbol, `render_positions` returns `Err(ViewError::DuplicateSymbolRow(symbol))` instead of emitting a duplicate row (lib.rs L540-545). EARS-002 is scoped to row-SHIFT mis-pairing, not duplicate-key detection/error semantics — this is unstated error-handling surplus, pinned in code alone (no direct unit test in formula.rs exercises the error path, but the guard and its ViewError variant are load-bearing production code).

The Tax tab (both the accrual band and reserve-summary band) is required to be 100% Cell::Value with zero formula cells (lib.rs render_tax; formula.rs `tax_tab_is_kernel_exact_not_live_formula`) — a whole-tab typing rule with no trace in SHEET-FORMULA-002's text, which is agnostic to which tabs carry formulas at all.
Quote Date is pinned at exact column index 12 (formula.rs `qcol == 12` assertion) — an exact schema position asserted by test, unstated by the spec text.

notes: Direction A (A1/A2/A3) converges tightly and CORRECTLY on the generic mechanism EARS-002 actually forces: DATA_START_ROW as a fixed compile-time constant (=2, matching the real `pub const DATA_START_ROW: u32 = 2`), row 1 structurally excluded from every write range (matching runtime/adapters.rs's `data_range` helpers and testkit's header-immutability assert), and full fresh regeneration of the formula range on every publish rather than incremental patching (matching render_positions's per-call recomputation and testkit's wholesale `existing.rows = tab.rows.clone()` replace). Because the real code fully honors this reading, Direction A surfaces no spec-forced-but-missing behavior. The three A runs' invented specifics (which column letters, whether a ColumnLayout struct vs raw indices, multi-letter column support) have no basis in the EARS-002 text itself and are unanimous-but-ungrounded assumption artifacts, not findings, per the classification rubric. Direction B, by contrast, independently and consistently reconstructs a large amount of load-bearing behavior that only the code+tests establish: the full 13-column formula catalogue, the zero-basis IF guard, the value/formula typing split and the tax-rate numeric-coercion trick, the quote-date locale-proof encoding, the duplicate-row error, the Tax-tab-all-values rule, and the column-12 pin for Quote Date. None of this is stated by, or reasonably inferable from, SHEET-FORMULA-002's terse anchoring/row-shift text. Since A shows no corresponding gap and B shows substantial, mutually-corroborated surplus, this is B-ONLY-DRIFT rather than BD-DRIFT — the two directions are not surfacing the same or related gap, they diverge: A stays faithful to (and matches) the narrow textual scope, while B's code-grounded reconstruction runs far ahead of what the spec text licenses.
